tutorial.label: CrazyGames publishing documentation
tutorial.note: Official requirements, SDK guides, testing tools, and launch workflow for web games.

detail: CrazyGames hosts browser games, with a separate developer portal and documentation for submission, technical requirements, SDK integration, and testing. Submissions receive QA review; Basic Launch and Full Launch have different requirements and availability. Supported web technologies span multiple engines. A playable portal build is a distribution artifact, not evidence that the complete game project is public or that AI developed it.
name: CrazyGames
summary: Play browser games and prepare web builds for CrazyGames submission, testing, and launch.

demo.note: Player storefront. Check each product's release status and supported systems; the store is not a playable project.

source.label: Platform listing is not game source
source.note: Game source and reuse rights must be checked independently of Epic Games Store availability.

tutorial.label: Epic Games Store publishing overview
tutorial.note: Official overview and FAQ for self-service distribution, developer setup, and store requirements.

detail: Epic Games Store offers a player storefront and publishing tools in the Epic Developer Portal for product pages, builds, offers, and updates. Distribution is engine-agnostic; using Unreal Engine is not a prerequisite. Developers still need account onboarding and must meet the store's content and product requirements. A store listing is distinct from a browser demo, an AI-development claim, or complete source code.

source.label: Platform listing is not game source
source.note: DRM-free describes distribution restrictions, not whether complete source or reusable assets are available.

tutorial.label: Submit a game to GOG
tutorial.note: Official submission page with an embedded developer form. Catalog inclusion requires a separate publishing decision.

detail: GOG is a curated digital game store with DRM-free releases and an optional desktop client. The official submission form is the developer entry point for proposing a game; submitting it does not guarantee acceptance or immediate publication. Verify each game's supported operating systems, edition, and release status. DRM-free distribution is different from publishing the game's source code.
name: GOG
summary: Discover DRM-free desktop releases and submit a game to GOG's curated catalog.

demo.label: Browse games on itch.io
demo.note: Independent game catalog with both browser and downloadable games. Availability and license vary by project.

source.label: Platform listing is not game source
source.note: Creators may publish source separately, but a game page or downloadable binary alone is not complete project source.

tutorial.label: Create your first itch.io page
tutorial.note: Official guide to project information, uploads, classification, publishing, and updates.

detail: itch.io lets creators manage game pages, screenshots, files, development logs, and updates. HTML5 builds can run in the browser; other releases can be provided as downloads with platform labels. A project's page can also contain a demo or work in development, so inspect the actual uploads and instructions. Publishing a playable build does not automatically make its source public.
name: itch.io
summary: Discover independent games and publish project pages with browser builds or downloadable releases.

demo.note: Game storefront. Check each product's release status, supported systems, and acquisition requirements; this is not an embedded browser demo.

source.label: Platform listing is not game source
source.note: Complete source must be verified separately for each game; a Steam listing does not supply it.

tutorial.label: Steamworks getting started
tutorial.note: Official publishing workflow covering partner setup, builds, store presence, and release review.

detail: Valve's Steam storefront distributes released games; Steamworks is the developer portal for onboarding, store presence, build uploads, testing, and updates. Publishing requires partner setup and review of the store page and build. A Coming Soon page, a demo, and a released game are different states. Steam availability does not establish AI authorship or public game source.
name: Steam
summary: Discover desktop games and use Steamworks to prepare store pages, builds, testing, and release.
